headline: Bitcoin heads for a sixth straight weekly loss as Anthropic's IPO pulls capital away from crypto
summary: A surging dollar and a high-profile tech IPO combined to push Bitcoin down 3.5% to $66,757, extending a losing streak that now spans six consecutive weeks. Solana fell hardest among large-caps, dropping 6.45%, while Zcash led all tracked assets lower at -9%. The one bright spot was Figure Heloc, a tokenized real-world asset that rose 4.53% — insulated from the crypto-specific selling pressure driving the rest of the market down.

winners.name: Figure Heloc
winners.catalyst: Figure Heloc bucked the broad market selloff, rising 4.53% as a tokenized real-world asset product insulated from the crypto-specific sentiment driving losses elsewhere. No specific news catalyst was identified in the provided data.

losers.name: Zcash
losers.catalyst: Zcash led losses among large-caps with a 9% decline, extending the broader market rout driven by a surging dollar and risk-off sentiment that has now pushed Bitcoin to a sixth consecutive weekly loss. Privacy coins may face additional headwinds amid ongoing regulatory scrutiny of new SEC nominations and prediction-market oversight discussions.

whyItMoved:
Two forces converged to push crypto lower today. First, a strengthening dollar made risk assets broadly less attractive — the same dynamic that has weighed on Bitcoin for six consecutive weeks. Second, Anthropic's blockbuster IPO is drawing capital away from speculative markets: when a high-profile private tech company opens to public investors, money tends to rotate out of higher-risk positions, and crypto is feeling that pull.

Beyond the macro pressure, analysts flagged structural market mechanics as a potential amplifier. The concern is that certain derivatives positions and automated liquidation triggers can turn a moderate selloff into a sharper one — meaning the current drawdown could overshoot what the underlying fundamentals would justify on their own.

Solana's 6.45% drop was the steepest among large-caps, consistent with its pattern of amplifying broad market moves in both directions. Hyperliquid fell 8.46% despite a separate report showing its derivatives open interest grew 80% in Q3 and surpassed Bybit, Kraken, and OKX — a reminder that strong platform metrics don't insulate a token from market-wide selling. The Fear & Greed index sits at 13 out of 100, deep in Extreme Fear territory, reflecting how far sentiment has deteriorated.
worthKnowing: The Senate Banking Committee is accelerating confirmation hearings for new SEC leadership, a development that could reshape crypto enforcement priorities and rulemaking direction in the months ahead.
The U.S. Department of Justice moved to seize $1.2 billion linked to the Binance hack, one of the largest crypto-related asset seizures pursued by federal prosecutors.
Hyperliquid's derivatives open interest grew 80% in Q3, pushing it past Bybit, Kraken, and OKX — though its HYPE token still fell 8.46% on the day alongside the broader market.
